newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SYNOPOSIS OF CZECH GOVT ECONOMIC MEASURES.
newsitem.headline: SYNOPOSIS OF CZECH GOVT ECONOMIC MEASURES.

text.p: The following is an unofficial synopsis of the Czech government's package of economic measures released on Wednesday:
ON MONETARY AND EXCHANGE RATE POLICY:

*There must be an inverse development in monetary and fiscal policy. Monetary policy, after its restriction in middle of the last year...must make a move in the opposite direction. Details of the change of the monetary policy are fully in the competency of the Czech National Bank and therefore are not discussed. The restriction of expenditures of the state budget shall be a very painful, but inevitable step.

*In public, the question of the exchange rate of the crown is discussed very intensively. Although we are aware that (some) subjects of the Czech economy would wish the rate higher or lower the signals coming to us from foreign exchange markets indicate to us that it would not be desirable to step out against the dominant trends on these markets. Any state intervention could be even counterproductive. Therefore we do not consider it rational to seek any exchange rate change.
ON LIMITING IMPORTS:

*To what extent the measures effecting aggregate demand shall themselves effect import and export flows which require a change in the foreseeable future. We follow from that only such measures which are acceptable from an international perspective, which may be announced as generally recognised measures for protection of the balance of payments of the country. After a consideration of arguments we consider it most suitable to implement so called import deposits which are understood as the deposit of non-interest deposits equalling a certain part of the valued of the imported goods, at a determined financial institution (bank), for a set period, and its freeing after the expiration of this set period. The importer shall have to prove to customs authorities the obligatory deposit as a condition for letting the goods into the country.

*We presume that this measure shall be projected to prices much less than alternative measures and that its effect on the limitation of imports shall be high. The advantage of this measure is also the fact that the WTO does not expect to discuss this measure prior to its implementation, but sets a four month period during which other WTO members must be consulted.

*Import deposits amounting to 20 percent of the value of the imported goods (or 60 pct, if a discussed alternative shall be approved) shall be imposed. The imposing of these deposits for a period of 180 days. Import deposits apply only to foodstuffs and consumer goods for one year with the possibility of changing this according to the development of the trade balance. Details of this measure shall be announced by a regulation of the Industry and Trade Ministry April 18.
ON STATE SPENDING:
Another part of the measures is the restriction of budget expenditures and their structure. The extent of restriction of expenditures is proposed at 25.5 billion crowns.
These restrictions will involve:
*Public sector wage growth limited to 7.3 percent from the 11.9 t growth in the approved state budget. The required result may be achieved by various methods, including cutting bonuses.
*Decreases in transfers to citizens by 3.3 billion crowns.

*Cutting of investment expenditures from the state budget by Kc 7.7 billion (ie. by 20 percent with the exception of transport infrastructure and the defence ministry, where the cuts shall be only by 8 pct)
*Cuts on non-investment subsidies by 1.5 billion crowns.
*Cuts of material expenditures of budget and contributor organisations by Kc 7.1 billion (i.e. by 15 pct).
*Cuts to budget reserves by Kc 0.6 billion (ie. by 52 pct).
*Cuts to the general account by Kc 1.1 billion.

The next task is ensuring a slowdown of growth of wage volume and possibly other non-wage benefits in state companies and in companies with a significant state share. This wage slowdown, including management wages, must be ensured by the entitiy excercising ownership rights. For the solution of similar problems in companies fully in the private state sector we shall pursue maximum cooperation and understanding of social partners -- trade unions and employers. We remind that the on-going decrease of inflation causes a decrease of real wages lower than the decrease of nominal wages.
INSTITUTIONAL MEASURES:

These changes react to problems -- especially in the micro- economic sphere -- with difficulties of the business sector on domestic and foreign markets, and in problems in the banking and capital markets. Their objective is to enforce strict abidance with laws, rules and regulations which is totally essential for the effective and balanced functioning of a market economy. It is therefore also the flexibility and effectiveness of the police, justice officials and all other bodies active in this area.

The proposed system and institutional measures must be performed as soon as possible. Some of them may begin to take effect immediately, others will require legislative changes. Their full effect will therefore come out only as time goes.
For the fulfilment of the objectives the following measures shall be taken:
*Accelerated completion of privatisation and strengthening of excercise of ownership rights of the state

*Speeding up the working out and announcement of the privatisation of companies and banks which are still in the hands of the state. To use, to achieve this end, combinations of standard privatisation methods which will ensure an optimal combination of speed, (financial) proceeds and sensitivity to the effects of privatisation; above all finding responsible owners of privatised property with a long-term interest in the prosperity of the companies. Therefore (privatised firms) will be put into the hands of successful managerial groups or strategic foreign partners. Proposals shall be presented by the Finance Ministry and relevant departments by the end of May.

*Strengthening the pressure for fulfilment of tasks of transformation institutions so their activity may be terminated as soon as possible. In between, their activity shall fully concentrate on the completion of privatisation. To enhance and professionalise executive bodies of these institutions in order to become truly effective bodies of the state as shareholders, not autonumous co-creators of state policy. The government shall (quarterly) deal with the activity and state tasks which they shall enforce in its practice. The proposals to be discussed in one month shall be prepared by the ministries of finance, agriculture and industry and trade.
*The excercising of ownership rights by the NPF in important companies shall be transfered to the ministries in cases, where this has not happened yet. This shall be performed within two months.

*By excercising shareholder rights to ensure that the compositions of bodies of companies with state participation, enable the state representatives in these companies to implement some government measures (especially pressure to a decrease in wage growth in relation to labour output).
*The pressure for accelerated liquidation or at least restructuring of the remainder state companies.
ON TRANSPARENCY AND STANDARDISATION OF CAPITAL AND FINANCIAL MARKETS:

*We must establish an independent securities commission. The task of this commission will be supervision of the capital markets. For this, a new law will be prepared, by May 13, by the Ministry of Finance for discussion by the goverment.

*To analyse the situation in the financial sector with the aim of making better relations between banks, investment funds and companies and to eliminate all conflicts of interests. This analysis should help limit the connections between banks, investment funds and companies. The Finance Ministry and central bank, together with Justice Ministry, should prepare within three months new proposals.
*Enforce very quickly any amendments to the law, which will lower tax deductable items and provisions for banks.

*Prepare an amendement to the law on investment funds and companies which will forbid funds and managers and employees of these investment companies from including relatives from owning shares in the investment and mutual funds administered by them or to own shares in firms which are in the funds' portfolio.

*Prepare an amendment to the law on investment funds and investment companies, which will forbid them from performing transactions with the property of the funds through related companies which create a conflict of interest.
*The above two amendments will be prepared within a month.
*Take measures to make prices on securities market more transparent. This will be done by the Finance Ministry together with Prague bourse and other bourses within three months.
*Clearly separate banks' loan operations from their portfolio management functions. At the same time to ban bank officials from being members of supervisory boards of firms.
*The Finance Ministry will immediately check the performance of banks as custodions. Shortfalls may be punished by the withdrawal of banking licences.
*Create stricter reporting requirements and strengthen capital sufficiency of subjects on the capital markets.
ON IMPROVEMENT OF CONDITIONS FOR PRIVATE BUSINESS AND EXPORT, THE PROTECTION OF THE DOMESTIC MARKET:
*Increase the possibility for write-offs of old uncollectable receivables to 20 percent from 10 percent.

*In making decisions on public orders, domestic supliers and producers will be preferred to foreign subjects. Producers will also be preferred to intermediaries. A minimum level of domestic participation should be set in tender conditions.
*Quickly change and strengthen the bankruptcy law.
*To increase the efficieny of regulation of natural monopolies including price issues.
*Enhance activities of the Czech Export Bank (CEB) and the export insurance company EGAP.
*Prepare an export support programme through EGAP, CEB and Konsolidacni Banka.
*Prepare minimal import prices in the agricultural sector in order to fight subsidised imports
*Impose acceptable seasonal import quotas on agricultural commodities and foodstuffs.
ON PUBLIC FINANCES:
*Regulate municipal indebtedness.
*Reduce the number of hospital beds and eliminate indebtedness of health care facilities.
*Introduce central budgetary financing and administration of state hospitals.
*Prepare rules for efficiency in spending in the public sector generally.
*Prepare a new law on the execution of ownership rights in remaining state holdings.
ON MEASURES AGAINST ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRIME:
*Set up a team formed from different state organs to fight criminality in the markets.
*Propose a law to create a special state organ to operate alongside the supreme state prosecution office to fight criminality in the banking sector.
*Immediately to investigate reasons for delays in prosecution of economic crime and delays in bankruptcies.
*New sections are to be added to the criminal code to deal with economic crime.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
